newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN DEPUTY PM DENIES PAEDOPHILIA ALLEGATION.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN DEPUTY PM DENIES PAEDOPHILIA ALLEGATION.

text.p: Belgian deputy prime minister Elio Di Rupo, responding to press reports that police were investigating a possible sex scandal, denied on Sunday that he had been involved in paedophile acts.
"The most foolish and most insulting information is circulating about me," Di Rupo, who is also economics and telecommunications minister in the ruling centre-left coalition, said in a statement.
"It would seem that I am the victim of a mix-up and confusion between events in my private life, which do nobody harm, and disgusting, outrageous acts which people want to attribute to me."
He said his behaviour reflected the values he defended: "In those values, my emotional life is a treasure which is only conceivable with responsible and consenting persons."
A leading opposition politician had called on the government earlier on Sunday to clear the air over a press report that Di Rupo was being investigated by police.

The Brussels prosecutors office, responding to a flurry of press reports of a probe into links between politicians and young homosexual prostitutes, had confirmed that police searched properties on Friday night but gave no details.

The deputy prime minister's name was first mentioned by a Dutch-language newspaper De Standaard, which said it had been told that "information pointed in the direction of socialist Elio Di Rupo," but there was no proof. It did not give its sources.

Herman De Croo, chairman of the opposition VLD liberal party, urged Christian-Democrat Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene on Sunday to make an early statement to parliament about this and an unrelated case in which Agriculture Minister Karel Pinxten has denied tax evasion and influence peddling.
"I am very worried," De Croo said in a panel discussion on Dutch-language BRTN television.
"In the past eight days, two names have been dropped, one clearly: Mr Pinxten; one slightly less clearly: Elio Di Rupo."
"Public confidence in the government has been shocked so seriously that this meeting (of parliament) is urgent."
The leader of the CVP Christian-Democrats, Marc Van Peel, however, warned against a "witch hunt" in which rumours were treated as facts.
Belgium is still reeling from the shock of an unrelated case in August when two young girls who had been abducted and sexually abused were rescued and the bodies of four other young girls were found.
